original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Which two-index pivots of the bandwidth-2 witness keep bandwidth b, and which only keep the inverse bound?
scope_change_reason: The scalar elimination already separates bandwidth from the inverse bound. The named next step is a two-index pivot on the same witness, including the prefix case where bandwidth does not grow.
bottleneck_link: Iterated elimination can reuse the inverse block identity without a bandwidth hypothesis on the complement. Reusing bandwidth b is valid for an invertible prefix and false for the tested interior pairs.
stop_rule: Stop once prefixes and the two interior pairs on this witness are settled. Do not start a boundary-order Gaussian elimination.
evidence: research/schur-prefix-bandwidth proves that an invertible prefix keeps bandwidth at most b, and exhibits two-index interiors of bandwidth 3 and 4 whose inverses remain inside the original Neumann bounds.
author: jwr
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from the Cursor coding agent in the argument, checker and writeup.

open_questions.question: After survivors are placed in boundary order, does one Gaussian interior elimination have bandwidth O(W)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: GAUSSIAN.md claims that bandwidth in a different order. These witnesses keep the original order.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one interior block and the stated boundary order, then measure the Schur bandwidth against W.
open_questions.blocked_by: No boundary-order elimination is computed in this package.

open_questions.question: Does an arbitrary middle interval, rather than a prefix, keep bandwidth at most b?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The prefix proof uses the cut at the left end. A middle interval can touch survivors on both sides.
open_questions.first_step: Eliminate indices 2 through 4 in this witness and compare the surviving bandwidth with b.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only prefixes and the two explicit interior pairs are checked here.
